17901069348612210.caption:
🌫️ “I’M HONESTLY SURPRISED WE’RE STILL ALIVE” — AIIMS DOCTOR WARNS ABOUT DELHI’S TOXIC AIR

Delhi’s post-Diwali air pollution has triggered serious concern among medical experts. Dr Vijay Hadda, Professor of Pulmonary Medicine at AIIMS Delhi, has warned that prolonged exposure to the city’s polluted air poses a significant risk to public health.

Speaking about the worsening conditions, Dr Hadda said he was surprised people were still managing to live with such air quality. He also highlighted that even otherwise healthy people were reporting persistent throat irritation and respiratory discomfort.

📊 How bad is the pollution?

• On November 9, Delhi recorded an AQI of 370, in the Very Poor category.
• Several neighbourhoods crossed the 400 mark, entering the Severe category.
• On November 11, the citywide AQI improved to 299, but several monitoring stations continued to report Very Poor air.

⚠️ Why does this matter?

Air pollution is not just a seasonal inconvenience. Prolonged exposure to particulate matter can worsen asthma and other respiratory conditions and increase cardiovascular risks. Children, older people and those with existing health conditions are particularly vulnerable.

Dr Hadda also pointed out that green crackers do not eliminate pollution: they reduce emissions by only around 30%, according to his remarks.

💬 Should tackling air pollution become a year-round public health priority rather than an annual emergency response?

📰 Sources: Reuters (9 November 2026); ANI / The Economic Times (9 November 2026); Mid-Day / PTI (11 November 2026).

⚠️ Important clarification: Innodata has not publicly confirmed the reported total number of affected employees or issued a detailed public explanation.

The incident raises serious questions about job security, transparent communication and employee support during sudden layoffs. For workers, losing access to employment records and payroll systems can make an already difficult situation even more stressful.

Goldman Sachs is tightening access to advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic's Claude Code and GitHub, following an internal review of productivity and risk management.

According to a Bloomberg report published on November 2, 2026, the bank has limited access mainly to engineering teams, ending broader access previously available to traders and bankers.

🔹 Most traders and bankers have reportedly lost access to these coding tools.

🔹 Engineering teams continue to have access.

🔹 Specialist employees known as strats, who work across trading, quantitative research and software engineering, are reportedly exempt.

🔹 Some employees had previously used AI tools to monitor trading activity, model market movements and create reports.

💡 Why did Goldman make this decision?

A Goldman spokesperson said the company evaluates AI tools based on factors including productivity and risk management before deciding which teams are best suited to use them.

The bigger picture

This is not a ban on AI across Goldman Sachs, nor is it a reported layoff. It reflects a growing shift towards controlled enterprise AI adoption, particularly in highly regulated industries.

The question is no longer just how widely companies can deploy AI, but who should have access and how responsibly it should be used.

17983263474138715.headline: ADANI GREEN’S MAHARASHTRA PROJECT COST REVISION UNDER SCRUTINY
17983263474138715.caption:
🚨 ADANI GREEN’S MAHARASHTRA PROJECT COST REVISION UNDER SCRUTINY

A major controversy has emerged over Adani Green Energy’s 1,500 MW Tarali pumped-storage project in Maharashtra’s Satara district.

According to The Indian Express, the project’s estimated cost was recorded as ₹5,675 crore in its February 2025 environmental clearance. However, a September 2026 affidavit submitted by the company cited ₹56.75 crore, describing it as an estimate based on analogous estimation.

The revision has significant implications for the wildlife conservation deposit linked to the project:

🔹 Earlier proposed deposit: ₹227 crore
🔹 Revised figure reported: Approximately ₹2.27 crore
🔹 Amount deposited so far: ₹56.75 lakh

🏢 What does Adani Green say?

The company has rejected allegations that it revised the figure to reduce statutory obligations. It says ₹56.75 crore referred only to site-investigation and survey expenses, while the State Board for Wildlife considered the total project cost to be ₹5,675 crore.

🔎 What happens next?

The Union Environment Ministry directed Maharashtra’s forest department to investigate the matter on priority. The department has also sought an explanation from the company.

Why does this matter?

The case raises important questions about transparency in large infrastructure projects, environmental clearances and the calculation of wildlife conservation obligations.

The investigation and official responses will be crucial in establishing the facts.

Sources: The Indian Express (13–14 November 2026); Adani Green Energy’s official statement.

18137598460741198.headline: 🏥 MEDICAL MILESTONE! AIIMS DELHI PERFORMS INDIA’S FIRST OPEN FETAL SPINAL SURGERY
18137598460741198.caption:
🏥 MEDICAL MILESTONE! AIIMS DELHI PERFORMS INDIA’S FIRST OPEN FETAL SPINAL SURGERY

Doctors at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, have achieved a major milestone by performing India's first open fetal surgery to repair a serious spinal defect in an unborn baby.

The six-hour procedure was performed on 12 November 2026, when the pregnancy was at 25 weeks.

🔬 What happened during the surgery?

The medical team repaired a condition called lumbosacral myelomeningocele, the most severe form of spina bifida. In this condition, the spinal cord and its protective coverings protrude through an opening in the developing spine.

Key highlights:

- 25 weeks: Stage of pregnancy during surgery.
- 6 hours: Duration of the operation.
- 30+ medical professionals: Doctors and nurses from multiple specialties participated.
- 5+ weeks: Dedicated planning and preparation before the procedure.
- Free treatment: The surgery was provided under the government's Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK).

💡 Why is this important?

Traditionally, this spinal defect is repaired after birth. Prenatal surgery aims to limit further damage to the developing spinal cord and may improve certain neurological outcomes in carefully selected cases.

However, doctors emphasise that this is not a complete cure. The mother and fetus will continue to receive close medical monitoring.

👏 A remarkable achievement for India's medical research, fetal medicine and multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

17988526757892114.caption:
🛡️ IIT GANDHINAGAR STUDENTS DEVELOP TRUSTGATE — AN AI SYSTEM TO DETECT CYBERATTACKS!

Two undergraduate students from IIT Gandhinagar, Miloni Thakkar (Computer Science and Engineering) and Mitwa Goswami (Electrical Engineering), have developed an AI-powered cybersecurity system called TrustGate to identify cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure.

🏆 International Recognition

Their innovation won the Second Prize at the Intel Cup – International Undergraduate Electronic Design Contest 2026, held at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China.

🔍 How does TrustGate work?

- It analyses network traffic and physical sensor data together.
- It identifies suspicious commands and unusual patterns.
- It can identify the equipment affected by a potential attack.
- It is designed to operate on embedded hardware without depending on cloud connectivity.

🌐 Why does it matter?

Critical infrastructure such as water treatment plants, power grids and manufacturing facilities increasingly need protection from cyber threats.

TrustGate aims to address a gap in conventional security systems by examining not just suspicious network activity, but also its possible physical consequences.

📌 What's next?

The system is currently a research prototype tested on a laboratory testbed. Further testing with live plant data, support for additional industrial protocols and security certifications are needed before real-world deployment.

👏 Congratulations to Miloni Thakkar and Mitwa Goswami for this impressive innovation!

🧬 TWINS, TWO BIOLOGICAL FATHERS: THE RARE SCIENTIFIC PHENOMENON!

A remarkable medical case from Brazil made headlines in 2022 after a 19-year-old woman reportedly gave birth to twins who had two different biological fathers.

How is this possible?

The phenomenon is known as heteropaternal superfecundation. It occurs when a woman releases two eggs during the same menstrual cycle, and each egg is fertilised by sperm from a different man following separate sexual encounters within a short period.

DNA testing confirmed that the twins shared the same mother but had different biological fathers.

🔬 The science behind it

- Both babies develop during the same pregnancy.
- The twins are fraternal, not identical.
- Each twin inherits DNA from a different biological father.
- DNA testing can establish the biological relationship.

Although medically documented, this phenomenon is extremely rare.

An extraordinary example of how genetics can reveal surprising facts about human reproduction!

On November 18, Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav inaugurated the first of nine units of the 1,920 MW Gandhi Sagar Pumped Hydro Storage Project in Neemuch district. Developed by Greenko Group, the project involves an estimated investment of ₹11,474 crore.

🔋 How will it work?

The facility will use two reservoirs to store energy. Surplus electricity, including solar and wind power, will pump water to an upper reservoir. When electricity demand rises, the stored water will flow down through turbines to generate power.

📊 Key highlights:

- Total planned capacity: 1,920 MW
- Estimated investment: ₹11,474 crore
- Total units: 9
- Generation at full capacity: Up to 6 continuous hours
- Full commercial operations targeted: June 2027

🌱 Why does it matter?

Solar and wind power are not always available when demand is highest. Pumped-hydro storage can help balance the electricity grid by storing surplus energy and releasing it when needed.

This project could strengthen Madhya Pradesh’s power infrastructure and support India's clean-energy transition.

📍 Location: Gandhi Sagar, Neemuch district, Madhya Pradesh

🚨 FACT CHECK: VIRAL AIRBAG HELMET VIDEO IS AI-GENERATED

A video circulating online claims to show a Chinese motorcycle helmet that deploys a giant airbag to protect a rider during a crash.

However, the footage is AI-generated, according to an India Today fact-check published on November 18, 2026. No verified Chinese product or prototype matching the viral video has been confirmed.

There is a real development behind the broader idea: motorcycle airbag vests and jackets already exist, and helmet-airbag concepts have also been explored. But the dramatic full-body airbag shown in this viral clip is not verified technology.

Why it matters: Road-safety innovations deserve attention, but misleading videos can create false impressions about products that may not exist.

Before sharing a technological breakthrough, check whether the product has been officially announced, tested and certified.
